## claude.ai Figma
The official Figma MCP server. Use this server whenever the user wants to create, generate, edit, implement, or sync any design, UI, screen, component, mockup, or visual — in Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or Figma Slides — and whenever the user mentions Figma or provides a figma.com URL.

This server bridges code and design in both directions, and supports designing from scratch using existing design systems and codebases.

CAPABILITIES:
- Read designs FROM Figma into code (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Write designs INTO Figma from code, intent, or existing components (use_figma, generate_figma_design, create_new_file, upload_assets)
- Bridge code and design via Code Connect (get_code_connect_map, add_code_connect_map, list_code_components, get_code_component_info)
- Create diagrams and FigJam content (generate_diagram, get_figjam)

WHEN TO USE THESE TOOLS:
- The user wants to create, mock up, or generate any UI, screen, component, or design — even if Figma isn't named
- The user wants to implement a design as code (design-to-code)
- The user wants to push a page, view, or component into Figma (code-to-design)
- The user wants to update, sync, or edit an existing Figma file
- The user shares a figma.com URL
- The user wants to build or extend a design system, design tokens, or component library
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

SKILLS (Prefer the skills shipped with the Figma plugin on the agent being used. If no Figma plugin is installed, use the skills served by the Figma MCP resource):
- /figma-use — MANDATORY before calling use_figma; fallback: skill://figma/figma-use/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-design — for translating an app page or layout into Figma; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-design/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-library — for building a design system in Figma from code; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-library/SKILL.md

# Versable App V4 — Enhancement Product Frontend

Product data enhancement platform for auto parts sellers. Next.js 16 fullstack app + FastAPI backend (`../backend/`).

## Code modularization — read before adding new files

Three module shapes: **feature** (`src/core/widgets-v2/`, `src/data/jobs/`),
**service** (`src/db/`), **catch-all utility** (`src/utils/` — rare; reuse must
be ≥3 callsites). Before creating a new file, check if an existing module
owns this concern. Before consolidating, confirm the pieces share a concern
(not just a directory).

Full framework + examples + repo-wide anti-patterns to flag:
[`docs/boring-technical-stuff/code-modularization.md`](docs/boring-technical-stuff/code-modularization.md)

## Comment style — read before writing docstrings

**Comments are for humans first, AI agents second, machines never.**

- Module / function docstrings open with what the thing IS in
  human terms, code-agnostic. Mechanism comes after.
- Speak from the caller's perspective, not the machine's.
- NEVER include `[claude@<ts>]` tags, "Phase N" / "Track X" /
  "Round Y" plan references, or "pre-fix / post-fix" archeology.
- Docstrings >8 lines are essays — break out to a doc and link.

Full rubric + checklist + before/after examples:
[`docs/boring-technical-stuff/comment-style.md`](docs/boring-technical-stuff/comment-style.md)

This **supersedes** the older "Code Comments — MANDATORY" rule below
that required `[claude@<timestamp>]` tags on every comment. That rule
was wrong — agent-authorship tags belong in git blame, not source.

## Tech Stack

Next.js 16.1.1 (App Router, Turbopack) | React 19.2.3 | TypeScript 5.x | Tailwind 3 + DaisyUI 4 | Jotai (client state) | TanStack Query 5 (server state, localStorage-persisted, 24h TTL) | Drizzle ORM + PostgreSQL | NextAuth v4 | Lexical editor | Stripe | AWS S3/SES | Sentry | Redis | Playwright (e2e) | Deployed on Vercel

## Commands

```bash
npm run dev          # Dev server (port 3006, Turbopack)
npm run build        # Build (runs DB migrations first)
npm run ts:build     # TypeScript check (no emit)
npm run lint:fix     # ESLint auto-fix
npm run prettier     # Format all files
npm test             # Playwright E2E (test:ui for interactive)
npm run db:generate  # Generate Drizzle migration after schema changes
npm run db:migrate   # Apply pending migrations
npm run db:studio    # Drizzle Studio GUI
```

Package manager: npm with `legacy-peer-deps=true`. **Node 22** (pinned in `.nvmrc` / `engines`) — run `dev`/`build` on Node 22 via [fnm](scripts/fnm.md) (`fnm use`); the pin is deliberate (Vercel runs 22, newer majors aren't supported), so don't bump Node to silence the dev-server version nudge.

## Directory Conventions

```
src/app/        App Router pages, layouts, API routes (/api/auth, credits, files, payment, token)
src/core/       Reusable UI: layout/, modal/, table/, query/, auth/, wizard/, button/
src/data/       Server-side data fetching — *.data.ts files (jobs, files, users, teams, etc.)
src/db/         Drizzle schema + methods. Migrations in drizzle/ (0000-0060+)
src/utils/      Hooks (25+), types, helpers, env config, routing.ts (Routes enum)
credit-worker/  Standalone Node.js credit processing worker (not part of Next.js app)
```

**Naming:** `*.data.ts` = server data | `*.server.ts` / `*.client.ts` = boundary files | `useQ*` / `useM*` = Query/Mutation wrappers | `/v2/` = active routes, `/v1/` = legacy

## API & Data Patterns

- **Route handlers** (`src/app/api/`): auth via `getServerSession(authOptions)`. Validate with Zod. Return consistent response shape.
- **Data layer** (`src/data/*.data.ts`): server-side functions for pages/routes. Never fetch in page components directly.
- **Mutations**: `useM` from `src/utils/hooks/use-m.ts` (wraps useMutation + toast). Invalidate cache explicitly.
- **Queries**: `useQ` from `src/utils/hooks/use-q.ts` (wraps useQuery with typed args). Keys via `src/utils/react-query.ts`.
- **Context**: `createKeyedContext` from `src/core/context/global-context.tsx` for typed React context.
- **Server actions**: `'use server'` directive required. Guard server-only modules with `withServer` from `src/utils/with-server.ts`.

## Key Gotchas

1. `force-dynamic` on root layout is intentional — documents intent for auth-gated app; `getServerSession()` already opts into dynamic rendering.
2. `_loading.tsx` underscore prefix is intentional — app uses component-level Suspense, not route-level skeletons.
3. lodash-es with Turbopack tree-shakes per-file. 100+ imports are fine; only Edge runtime compat matters.
4. Always grep import sites before flagging components as unused — comment state can be misleading.
5. TanStack Query is NOT persisted — `AppWrapperClient` uses plain `QueryClientProvider`. Still invalidate explicitly after mutations (in-memory cache retains for `gcTime`).
6. React Compiler (`babel-plugin-react-compiler`) is enabled, but **write code as if it isn't there** — manual `useMemo` / `useCallback` stays where it makes performance or syntax sense (multi-step expressions, profiled-expensive work, compiler-off safety). The compiler is a safety net, not a directive to strip existing memoization. See `docs/decisions/ADR-005-react-compiler-enabled.md`.
7. `/_info` admin routes are NOT admin-gated at the proxy — `src/proxy.ts` only enforces token-presence (any logged-in user passes). Admin gating happens entirely in the route handler via `routeWrapper`. HTTP Basic Auth is still TODO at `src/proxy.ts:20`. See `docs/known-pitfalls/info-routes-no-admin-check-at-proxy.md`.
8. Always run `npm run db:generate` after any `src/db/schema/*.ts` change.
9. Test data transforms on small samples first — past bugs include `[object Object]` in Excel exports.
10. Read `gotchas.md` in the project root for additional known pitfalls.

## React Debugging — Fiber Snatcher

Tool at `~/.local/bin/fiber-snatcher` provides deterministic state/dispatch/error access to this dev app. Prefer it over hand-rolled `browser_evaluate` for any state read or dispatch. Keep the daemon running across tool calls (~50ms reuse vs ~1.5s relaunch).

Key commands: `status`, `doctor`, `state '<selector>'`, `errors --since Xm`, `shoot --name X`. Setup config lives at `.fiber-snatcher/config.json`; auth bypass uses Pattern A in repo's `USAGE.md` §3a. Full operating rules: `~/Code/Claude/invasion-of-the-fiber-snatchers/CLAUDE.md`.

## Slack MCP — `slack-bot`

Always-on MCP defined in `.mcp.json`. Bot: `versable_docs_mcp`, token env: `SLACK_MCP_XOXB_TOKEN`. Channel IDs and full scope/limit reference: see memory `reference_slack_mcp.md`. Key channels: #versable-engineering `C07KMQR3NPN` · #scraper-requests `C09LUH5EFUL` · #dev-sync `C0AQ4JZBNJ3` · #dev-logs `C08JZAHHRRU`.

**Hard limit:** `search:read` requires a user token (xoxp); bot tokens cannot call `search.messages`. **Token rotation:** reinstalling the Slack app issues a new xoxb token — update `SLACK_MCP_XOXB_TOKEN` or scopes break silently.

## Dev-server memory — local tooling (opt-in, not CI)

Turbopack dev memory grows as routes compile and never releases (~85% native), so a long session creeps toward maxing out RAM. Two **local-only, opt-in** tools (not wired into CI):

- **`npm run dev-safe`** — idle-gated auto-restart that caps the dev server's RAM. Docs: [`scripts/dev-guard.md`](scripts/dev-guard.md).
- **`perf/`** — composable toolkit (server / measure / logs / drive) to quantify it, plus a one-shot benchmark `npm run perf:bench`. Built for agent-driven measure→change→re-measure investigation. Docs: [`perf/README.md`](perf/README.md).

**Agent directive — do NOT auto-run or assume these.** Never invoke `dev-safe`, `perf:bench`, or the `perf/` primitives on your own. Act on them only when the user explicitly asks. If a dev hits dev-server memory/perf pain you MAY surface that these exist (a one-line explanation + benefit) and let them decide — but never treat this capability as a default for this repo.

## Claude Skills & Rules

- **22 skills** in `.claude/skills/` — `/pick-skill` to browse. Key: `/new-query`, `/new-migration`, `/arch-qa`, `/create-report`, `/pr-review`, `/type-audit`, `/catchup`, `/context-prime`
- **3 context rules** in `.claude/rules/` — `api-routes.md`, `db-schema.md`, `server-actions.md` (auto-activate by file path)
- **Runtime notes**: `.claude/skills/runtime-notes.md` — prepend insights after each session
- **Project index**: `.claude/project-index.md` — full architecture reference
- **Improvements backlog**: `.claude/improvements.md` — known config gaps
- **Feature plans**: `.claude/whiteboard/<feature-name>/PLAN.md`
- **Widget v2 docs**: `src/core/widgets-v2/docs/` — master plan, research patterns, audit synthesis reports for the generic widget system
- **Component audits**: `.claude/whiteboard/component-audit/` — per-component audit files + FRAMEWORK.md methodology
- **MCP servers** disabled at rest. Use `/mcp-use` to enable. Catalog: `.claude/mcp-catalogue.json`
- **Doc-writing guidelines**: `.claude/doc-writing-guidelines.md` — MANDATORY when editing any `.md` under `docs/`. Pairs with the global guidelines at `~/.claude/doc-writing-guidelines.md`. Read both before drafting or rewriting a product doc.
- **Docs placement guide**: `.claude/notes/docs-placement-guide.md` — MANDATORY before _adding_ a doc under `docs/`. Routes task type → which docs to read + where to write. Pairs with `docs/structure.md` (sidebar map + rationale).

## Component & Utility Lookup — MANDATORY

Before writing any new component, hook, or utility function, **read `docs/boring-technical-stuff/frontend/ui-widgets/_index.md`** and check the Quick Decision Matrix and category tables. If an existing item covers the use case (even partially), use it. If it needs a small extension, confirm with the user before modifying. Only create new code when no existing item fits.

For detailed API reference on any item, read its linked doc file in `docs/boring-technical-stuff/frontend/ui-widgets/<bucket>/`. Use `/lookup` to search programmatically.

## No New Packages Without Checking — MANDATORY

**Do not `npm install` new dependencies** without first verifying that the functionality isn't already available in the project's existing packages. This project has 100+ dependencies — the answer is usually already installed.

Before proposing a new package:

1. Check `package.json` for existing packages that cover the use case
2. Search `src/` for existing implementations of the pattern you need
3. Check if the framework (Next.js, Playwright, TanStack Query, etc.) already provides the feature natively

**Incident context:** `@testing-library/react` and `@testing-library/dom` were installed locally for unit tests on a `use-query-sync` hook, but Playwright (already installed) handles all E2E testing, and Vitest (if needed for unit tests) ships its own DOM utilities. The extra packages were never committed but polluted the local `node_modules` and `package.json`. Always exhaust what's already in the dependency tree before reaching for `npm install`.

## Code Style — Avoid Nested Ternaries in JSX

When a JSX prop or value requires more than 2 branches, **extract it into a `useMemo` with a `switch` statement** instead of chaining ternaries. Deeply nested ternaries are hard to read and easy to break.

**Bad** (4-level ternary in JSX):

```tsx
next={step === "S1" ? { ... } : step === "S2" ? { ... } : step === "S3" ? { ... } : undefined}
```

**Good** (extracted to useMemo):

```tsx
const footerNext = useMemo(() => {
  switch (step) {
    case "S1": return { ... };
    case "S2": return { ... };
    case "S3": return { ... };
    default: return undefined;
  }
}, [step, ...deps]);

// In JSX:
<ModalFooter next={footerNext} />
```

This applies to any prop with 3+ conditional branches — not just footer configs.

## Code Style — Early Returns Over Top-Level Ternaries

When a component's return has a top-level ternary (`condition ? <A/> : <B/>`), use an early return instead. This flattens the main render and avoids unnecessary nesting.

**Bad:**

```tsx
return (
  <>
    {!data.length ? (
      <EmptyState />
    ) : (
      <Table ... />  // 100+ lines deep inside ternary
    )}
  </>
);
```

**Good:**

```tsx
if (!data.length) return <EmptyState />;

return (
  <>
    <Table ... />
  </>
);
```

## Code Comments — MANDATORY

**Keep comments short, plain, and only when the code isn't self-explanatory.** Do not use decorative banners like `// ─── Section ────────────────────`. A simple `// Section name` is enough.

**Every comment Claude writes must start with `[claude@<timestamp>]`** so the user can distinguish agent-authored comments from human ones. Use ISO-like short format: `[claude@2026-03-31]`.

**Examples of good comment style** (from this codebase):

```ts
// Heavy extraction — kept explicit despite React Compiler being enabled due to cost
// Declared before callParseFile so onSuccess can initialize sheetMappings
// Credit keys available for custom parts — union of job-expected keys + fallback
// File part — find by current (possibly overridden) referenceId
```

**Do NOT write:**

```ts
// ── S3: Review Credits ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// ── Checkbox ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// ── Part Number (editable for all parts) ─────────────────────────────
```

**Instead write:**

```ts
// [claude@2026-03-31] S3: Review Credits
// Checkbox
// Part Number (editable for all parts)
```

Only add comments where the logic isn't obvious from the code. Inline JSX comments (`{/* ... */}`) follow the same rules.

## GitHub Actions — `.github/` Conventions

Non-trivial scripts and all HTML/CSS files belong in `.github/scripts/`, not inlined inside `run:` blocks.

**Why:** YAML block scalars (`run: |`) require all content lines to be indented to the block level. Python code and HTML at column 0 terminate the block scalar early, silently producing broken workflows that pass YAML parsing but misbehave at runtime.

**Pattern:**

- Shell one-liners: inline in `run:` is fine
- Short multi-line strings (≤3 lines, no `#` at start): `printf '...\n...\n'` — never bash heredocs
- Python scripts (> ~5 lines): `.github/scripts/<name>.py`, called via `python3 "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/.github/scripts/<name>.py"`
- HTML pages: `.github/scripts/<name>.html`, copied via `cp "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/.github/scripts/<name>.html" <dest>`
- Bash scripts (> ~10 lines): `.github/scripts/<name>.sh`

**Current scripts in `.github/scripts/`:**

- `dashboard-header.html` / `dashboard-footer.html` — E2E report dashboard template (split for `envsubst`)
- `portal-index.html` — Root gh-pages portal page (links to `/e2e/`, `/docs/`, `/docs-raw/`)
- `docsify-index.html` — Docsify SPA shell for `/docs/` (includes client-side frontmatter parser + og: meta updater)
- `generate-sidebar.py` — Generates `_sidebar.md` from the docs file tree

**Related rules:**

- **Don't add `set -euo pipefail` to a working script in the same change as a refactor.** It exposes pre-existing latent failures and you'll attribute the breakage to the refactor.
- **Concurrency `group:` should match actual exclusion needs**, not "this is a related workflow". Workflows that touch independent paths and have `git pull --rebase` should use separate groups.
- **`git add .` does NOT remove files.** For path migrations on a deployment branch, explicit `git rm` is required and any in-flight workflows that pre-cloned the branch will resurrect old paths on push.

**RCA:** [`docs/workflows/gh-pages-restructure-rca.md`](docs/workflows/gh-pages-restructure-rca.md) — full incident report from the April 2026 gh-pages restructure, with every issue traced to root cause and prevention rule. Read before touching this area.

## E2E Test Suite Versioning

The E2E suite version is defined in `test/test.utils.ts` as `E2E_SUITE_VERSION` and printed in every run summary. Bump it when making changes to test files or the CI workflow:

- **Patch** (v2.1 → v2.2): Bug fixes, selector updates, timeout adjustments, adding/removing tags, config tweaks
- **Minor** (v2.2 → v3.0): New test modules, structural changes to the describe tree, new shared helpers, workflow architecture changes
- **No bump needed**: Doc-only changes, CLAUDE.md updates, whiteboard/plan files

## Task Framing — newness × blast-radius

Before starting a non-trivial task, classify it on TWO axes. The
combination determines mode. Code volume is NOT the signal.

1. **Newness**

   - new surface — greenfield page, prototype, fresh feature
   - existing surface — refactor, polish, bug-fix on shipped UI

2. **Blast radius**
   - low — admin-only, internal, lab routes, behind a flag
   - high — core user journeys, most-used pages, billing/auth

Mode by quadrant:

- new + low → MAXIMALIST: design-first, ambitious scope.
  Think product. Surface user-stories before
  writing JSX. Take risks. Exercise new patterns
  and primitives. Don't just clone the source.
- new + high → MEASURED: design-first but ship gated. Prove
  on a slice before broadening. Flag-guard.
- existing + low → NORMAL: scoped refactor. Parity test. Mid risk.
- existing + high→ SURGICAL: minimal change, prove safety.
  "Surgical" still means deeply considered within
  the scope — surface adjacent concerns
  (a11y, edge states, related interactions) and
  ASK which are in scope. Don't just do the
  literal ask.

**Maximalist within enhancement-product has a ceiling.** This is an
org product with real customers and a shared codebase. Even MAXIMALIST
mode means "explore freely in code, but every change is human-reviewed
before persistence" — see the absolute commit rule below. Maximalist is
NOT "rewrite the information architecture" or "introduce experimental
patterns to core flows." It IS: think product-first, surface admin/internal
affordances the source doesn't have, exercise the widget surface fully.

**Signals to detect MAXIMALIST license in task text:**

- "use as a canary", "take more control"
- "no harm if it breaks", "fresh page", "new page"
- "use this as an opportunity to...", "from scratch"
- admin-only or lab-only routing in path

**Signals to detect SURGICAL constraint:**

- "minimal change", "scoped to X", "don't touch Y"
- "core flow", "most-used", "production"
- any user-facing primary journey, any auth/billing surface

When in doubt, ASK before defaulting to NORMAL. Cost of asking is
30 seconds; cost of mis-framing is hours of wrong-direction iteration.

## New-page checklist — MANDATORY before writing JSX

For new surface (especially MAXIMALIST mode), before writing the
first JSX, write a short answer to each in conversation:

1. Who is the user (role, context, what brought them here)?
2. What are their TOP 3 actions on this page? (primary)
3. What are their NEXT 3 actions? (secondary)
4. What existing components in `src/core/widgets/` + the docs index
   `docs/boring-technical-stuff/frontend/ui-widgets/_index.md`
   address those actions? Run `/lookup` or grep before answering.
5. If cloning a source page (e.g., DHV3): what does THIS user need
   that the source does NOT? List 2-3 role-specific affordances.
6. Cross-links: which other admin pages or data areas should this
   page surface quick links to?

Get user confirmation on this list. If they say "go", that's
confirmation. If they push back, the list saved a wasted iteration.

"Feature parity with X" is never a complete design target — the
source page exists for a different user.

## New-page registration — MANDATORY for ALL new pages

**A new page is invisible until registered.** Whenever you create a new page
file (`page.tsx` under `src/app/`), you MUST register it in routing + the
appropriate link map before declaring the work done. This applies to **every
surface** — normal user pages, admin pages, lab pages.

**Do NOT skip registration unsolicited.** If the user explicitly says "skip
registration" or "URL-only, don't add to nav", honor that. Otherwise: ASK
when something is unclear, then register.

**Before writing JSX, ASK the user** (with sensible defaults suggested) to
fill in any of these you can't infer from context:

| Field              | What to ask                            | Default to suggest                                                      |
| ------------------ | -------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Surface            | Normal / admin / lab?                  | infer from URL prefix; ask if ambiguous                                 |
| Title              | What appears in the sidebar            | snake-case → Title Case of the route slug                               |
| Description        | One sentence on what the page does     | one-line summary of the work brief                                      |
| Group (admin only) | App Data / Debug / Lab / Teams / Admin | see decision below                                                      |
| Icon               | Which `IconFor` entry                  | scan `src/utils/icons.ts` for a semantic match                          |
| Color (admin only) | tw color or hex                        | `getTwColor("slate")?.[500]` for utility, brand color for branded tools |
| Order (admin only) | grouping number                        | match the closest sibling's `order`                                     |

If you have everything from context, register without asking. If anything is
ambiguous, ASK once with the defaults pre-filled — the user can confirm or
override in one message.

**Group choice (admin pages):**

- **App Data** — first-class admin tooling for product entities (jobs,
  payment plans, teams).
- **Debug** — observability of production data (Redis Cache, Credit
  Dispatch, App Info).
- **Lab** — experimental / dev-tool / "exercise the system" pages. **If
  you're inventing a tool to verify or play with a feature, it's Lab, not
  Debug.** Debug is for inspecting real production data.
- **Teams** / **Admin** — top-level admin nav.

If none fit, ASK before inventing a new group.

### Pattern A — normal user-facing page (`/<route>`)

```ts
// 1. src/utils/routing.ts
export const Routes = {
  // ...
  MyPage: "/my-page/",
} as const;
// add to AppSettingsRoutes if it should appear in user-side nav

// 2. src/utils/core/app-links.data.ts — add the AppLinkItem
//    (search the file for an existing user-facing entry to mirror)
```

### Pattern B — admin page (`/admin/*`, App Data / Debug / Teams group)

```ts
// 1. src/utils/routing.ts
export const AdminRoutes = {
  // ...
  MyAdminPage: "/admin/my-admin-page/",
} as const;
export const AdminSettingsRoutes = [
  // ...
  AdminRoutes.MyAdminPage,
];

// 2. src/app/admin/admin.data.ts
{
  link: AdminRoutes.MyAdminPage,
  title: "My Admin Page",
  description: "What it lets the admin do",
  icon: "Redis",                           // IconFor key (string)
  group: "Debug",                          // matches AdminGroup union
  color: getTwColor("slate")?.[500],
  order: 41,                               // match closest sibling
}
```

```ts

export const LabRoutes = {
  // ...
  MyLabPage: "/lab/my-lab-page/",
} as const;

// 2. src/app/lab/lab.utils.ts — append to ListLabProjects
{
  link: LabRoutes.MyLabPage,
  title: "My Lab Page",
  description: "What this experimental tool does",
  icon: IconFor.Log,                       // IconFor reference (NOT a string)

```

The single `ListLabProjects` entry fans out to: admin sidebar Lab group
(via the spread in `admin.data.ts`), `app-links.data.ts` search/nav (via
`MapLabRoutes`), and `/lab/page.tsx` cards.

**Does NOT apply** when editing an existing page that's already in the
sidebar map. Editing existing entries doesn't trigger this rule.

## UI changes — actually exercise the interaction

The `For UI or frontend changes, start the dev server and use the
feature in a browser` rule under "Doing tasks" applies HARD here:

For any UI task that introduces a new interaction (click, hover,
selection, modal open, drag, toggle), you MUST exercise that
interaction at least once before declaring done. fiber-snatcher
screenshots do NOT count — they are read-only verification. If
you cannot click in the current environment, say so explicitly and
ask the user to verify the specific interaction.

Common interaction bugs hidden by screenshot-only verification:

- row-click vs cell-click target mismatches
- checkbox double-fire (event bubbles through label + input)
- focus traps in dropdowns / modals
- keyboard nav broken
- hover states not applied or applied to wrong element

## /designer-reviewer skill — calibration note

This skill is calibrated for a charcoal-terminal aesthetic used in
OTHER projects (pm2-manage, visualize-claude, etc.). enhancement-product
is light-mode SaaS. The skill's FP-1 (Dark Mode Default) finding
does NOT apply here. Use the skill for confirming polish gaps you've
already identified, not as a primary design judge. If its findings
keep insisting on dark mode or charcoal tokens, ignore those findings

# Rule — Don't regex-match error messages for selector flow

**Scope:** any frontend code that branches on the _content_ of a backend error string to decide which user-facing message / UI state to render.

## The rule (one line)

If your code does `/some-text/i.test(err.message)` (or `.includes(...)`, `.match(...)`, `.startsWith(...)`) on a backend-supplied error string to drive a `switch` / `if` / route, **stop**. Replace with a stable structured code on the envelope.

## Why

A regex match couples the frontend's branching logic to the backend's literal English string. When the backend rephrases the message (clearer wording, typo fix, i18n, log scrub), the frontend silently falls through to the generic case. The bug is invisible at compile time, invisible at request time, and only surfaces when a user sees the wrong message — usually long after the deploy that broke it.

Substring collisions are also real: `"job is empty"` matches both an intentional empty-input check and a stray log line about an empty `job.metadata` field.

## What to do instead

Carry a flag, not a sentence:

1. **Backend:** raise a structured exception that carries a stable string `code` plus optional `context` data. In this repo:

   ```python
   raise JobOutputCause(
       JobOutputCauseCode.download_template_not_found,
       f"Configuration data not found for download template {template_key}",
       context={"template_key": template_key},
       status_code=400,
   )
   ```

   The envelope picks up `cause_code` + `cause_context` fields automatically (see `backend/lib/jobs/formats/errors.py`).

2. **Frontend:** branch on the code, interpolate from the context:

   ```ts
   switch (err.cause_code) {
     case "download_template_not_found":
       return `Template "${err.cause_context?.template_key}" not found.`;
     // ...
   }
   ```

3. **Mirror the codes in BOTH places.** Backend `JobOutputCauseCode` enum and frontend `JobOutputCauseCode` literal union must stay in sync. A new variant is a two-file change.

## When string matching IS acceptable

- **Display only**, never selector logic — e.g. searching the message for a known PII pattern to redact it before logging. The match controls _rendering_, not _which branch runs_.
- **Last-resort fallback** when the upstream system is genuinely external and you have zero control over its envelope (third-party SDK with no error codes). Even then — wrap your matcher behind a single helper, and treat any new match as tech debt.

## Verify

```bash
rg -n "(test|match|includes|startsWith)\(.*err\.(message|cause_message)" frontend/src
# Expect: zero matches, except in display-only or upstream-fallback helpers
```

## Related

- `backend/lib/jobs/formats/errors.py:JobOutputCause` — the structured cause class
- `frontend/src/data/jobs.data.ts:runTransformMessage` — flag-driven renderer (was regex-based pre 2026-05-04)

# Server Actions & Server Component Rules

These rules activate for files in `src/app/` and `src/data/`.

## Server Actions

When creating a Server Action:

1. **Always add `'use server'` directive** at the top of the file or function
2. **Validate input with Zod** — never trust client-supplied data
3. **Check auth** before performing any mutation:
   ```typescript
   const session = await getServerSession(authOptions);
   if (!session?.user) throw new Error("Unauthorized");
   ```
4. Return a typed result — use a discriminated union `{ success: true, data } | { success: false, error }` pattern

## Data Files (`*.data.ts`)

- `src/data/*.data.ts` files are Server Component data access functions — server-only
- These functions are called directly in page/layout Server Components, never in Client Components
- Always mark with `import "server-only"` or use `withServer` guard from `src/utils/with-server.ts`
- Do not call these from `route.ts` — they're for RSC only; use `src/db/` queries in API routes

## Server/Client Boundary

- **Server files:** `*.server.ts`, `*.data.ts` — can import from server-only packages
- **Client files:** `*.client.ts`, `'use client'` components — cannot import server-only modules
- If a file needs to work in both contexts, it must be isomorphic (no server-only imports)
- Use `withServer` from `src/utils/with-server.ts` to guard server-only modules

## TanStack Query Invalidation

After any mutation (Server Action or API route), invalidate the relevant TanStack Query keys on the client:

```typescript
// In the useM hook caller:
onSuccess: () => {
  queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: QueryKeys.resource(id) });
};
```

Failing to invalidate leaves stale data in TanStack Query's in-memory cache (retained for `gcTime`). Note: this app uses a plain `QueryClientProvider` in `app-wrapper.client.tsx` — there is **no** `PersistQueryClientProvider`, so the cache is not persisted to localStorage. Explicit invalidation is still required after every mutation.

**1. `enableModifierKey` now works.** When set, drag only engages while the key is held. The gate lives in `onMouseDown` (line 108): `if (usesModifierKey && !computeModifierAllows(e))` bails out before starting a drag. Absent → always-on, unchanged.

**2. `disableModifierKey` (legacy) preserved.** Folded into the same `computeModifierAllows` check — Shift-held still sets `isSkip` and skips the drag, exactly as before. The modal's `isSkip`-based cursor logic is untouched.

**3. `isDragScrollEnabled` is now correct** (line 176): `!disabled && modifierAllowsDrag`. Previously it was just `!disabled`, so for `enableModifierKey` it would have falsely shown a "grab" cursor when the key wasn't held. `modifierAllowsDrag` is a reactive state driven by `keydown`/`keyup`, so the cursor flips the instant Cmd goes down/up — no mouse movement needed. This is what `generic-table.tsx:256` already consumes for its cursor, and what helper messages can read.
